sources.note: This work describes none: the note is a political/ethnographic history of the Ntem village (Nsungli/Wiya group, Bamenda division, British Cameroons); no language is described. No statement about word stress, accent or tone anywhere in the 17 pages (a full-text search for stress/accent/syllable/vowel/phonetic: no hits; 'Tonebit' is a chief's name). The article is a compilation of colonial reports (Hunt 1920, Bamenda Quarterly Report 1922, Hawkesworth 1923, Drummond-Hay 1924, Carpenter's Kaka-Ntem Intelligence Report) and oral histories (Wiya, Ntem, Rom, Mbem) on the Ntem chief's claims and the…

sources.citation: Leroy, Jacqueline. 1994. Le Mbam-Nkam ou Est-Grassfield. Africana Linguistica 11: 135-140. doi:10.3406/aflin.1994.949
sources.note: Group-level survey: proto-Mbam-Nkam verb roots split H vs L, a distinction said to survive in all languages surveyed; noun roots LL, HH, LH, HL plus a floating final tone. No Yamba tone system given.

tone.quote: Tons: L'étude des tons n'a pas posé de problèmes majeurs, les correspondances étant, dans leur ensemble, régulières. Les racines verbales de la proto-langue se répartissent en deux groupes H (haut) et B (bas). On retrouve cette distinction dans toutes les langues présentes. Les racines nominales se répartissent en quatre groupes : -B B, -H H, -B H et -H B. L'étude porte sur les noms dans leur forme de citation. … la présence d'un préfixe nominal à ton bas et T final (bas ou haut), surtout lorsque ce ton n'a pas dans les langues actuelles de support segmentai propre …
tone.translation: Tones: The study of the tones raised no major problems, the correspondences being, on the whole, regular. The verb roots of the proto-language fall into two groups, H (high) and B (low). This distinction is found in all the present-day languages. The noun roots fall into four groups: -L L, -H H, -L H and -H L. The study bears on nouns in their citation form. … the presence of a low-toned noun prefix and a final T (low or high), especially when that tone has no segmental support of its own in the present-day languages …
tone.summary: Group-level survey: proto-Mbam-Nkam verb roots split H vs L, a distinction said to survive in all languages surveyed; noun roots LL, HH, LH, HL plus a floating final tone. No Yamba tone system given.

sources.note: Per Leroy 1994 (Africana Linguistica 11: 137-139), this is the report of Hyman's 1978 GTBG survey reconstructing proto-Mbam-Nkam phonology from a 300-word list over 62 lects (seven of them Yamba: Sih, Kaka, Kwak, Mfe, Nkot, Ntong, Ntem per Glottolog language code); it has a tone chapter (tone correspondences 'regulieres', proto verb roots H vs B, noun roots B.B/H.H/B.H/H.B, floating final T; correspondence table for *B.H at p. 69), so Yamba lect tone reflexes are very likely tabulated there. No Yamba-specific tone statement verified.
